definition: Incident identifier from incident-register.csv. INC-EXAMPLE-NN is reserved for fictional training rows and must say FICTIONAL in notes.

FACTOR: the adjudicator's consolidated factor list, one row per incident and factor, frozen before the EOD sample is drawn. BASELINE: one baseline coder's judgement for one factor and one method. AIDCF_EOD: estimated operational detectability for AIDCF on a sampled factor. GAP_DISPOSITION: the disposition of one baseline-only (class c) pair.
Pseudonymous coder code, as in coding-sheet.csv. On FACTOR, GAP_DISPOSITION and RECONCILED rows, the adjudicator's code.
A and B are independent baseline codings of the same method; RECONCILED is the adjudicated record. FACTOR and GAP_DISPOSITION rows are always RECONCILED. Metrics use RECONCILED rows only.
Y if the coder declared independence from the framework author. Baseline coders must be Y.
Coder's familiarity with this incident's cause before coding, declared before reading the dossier.
Factor identifier from the consolidated list. Every RECONCILED CONTROL factor in coding-sheet.csv for an incident in this sheet must have a FACTOR row.
Who first surfaced the factor. ADJUDICATOR: added from the dossier by the adjudicator, not by either side. Results are reported for all factors, for AIDCF or BOTH, and for BASELINE or BOTH.
Coder IDs and dossier passages the factor came from.
As in coding-sheet.csv, and must match the consolidated factor there. Only STATED_KNOWN and DISCOVERABLE factors enter the comparison.
As in coding-sheet.csv and must match it. Only PRE_REVEAL factors enter the comparison.
Y if the factor is in the EOD sample. Set only from --draw-eod-sample output, which is refused once any detection judgement exists. Must equal the seeded draw from the locked frame.
Comparator method. Only methods with pilot_status ACTIVE in baselines.csv may be judged; the others are NOT_EVALUATED in this run and are never coded NOT_APPLICABLE.

definition: Same scale and meanings as the AIDCF side, plus two baseline values. OUT_OF_SCOPE: the method declares the factor outside its scope; counts as a miss. NOT_APPLICABLE: the method does not apply to this incident; the pair drops out.
